There are also people that see voting as "I agree" or "I disagree".

This is it 90% of the time. People get a sense of "okay my opinions are right" if they see everything they agree with upvoted.

Most of those downvotes, particularly on themed subs (like Linux, AMD) and especially on big default subs (funny, video, wtf, gaming), are from bots.

As you've probably noticed, top comments are usually one of the first post in a thread.
New thread gets posted, first comments (usually puns, jokes - low effort upvote bait) get the early upvotes, and then each time someone visits the thread, they see those early comments on top. Because people are sheep, they'll upvote those top comments further, and won't read past first 100 comments. This process repeats, and you get this monstrous thread with over 1000 replies, where 9-10 comments (earliest ones) have more upvotes than the rest of the thread combined. It's a snowball effect.

Ad companies, attention whores and agenda pushers can exploit that fact, and run several bots in a rented botnet. What those bots will do is find threads containing particular keywords in title, post automated witty reply (related to keyword - it's easier than it sounds) asap, or message owner, who will post something manually, and then use other bots to upvote that comment, while downvoting the rest. This pushes it to the top, and keeps the rest on the bottom. Because of above mentioned snowball effect, "engineered" comments gets to the top 10. Additional boost can be gained from gilding it (so it's distinguishable even in top 10).

It's an old procedure, and cannot be fought against on reddit at least, because admins not only know of it, but also endorse it (giving comment gold earns them money, duh). Powerposters never get caught (there are several powerposters on voat, or at least I assume they have some objective in posting in every random thread, because I don't think they have no life and spend whole day here).

You can't downvote on Voat until you have 100 CCP (aka comment karma over there), so only people who make a habit of posting interesting comments even get the chance. There are also simply more users, so a post here with –1 or so might be –10 on a thread over there because more people pass through and vote. I also think that Voat slowly gives you more downvotes to use per day, so even the normal commentators can't kill an entire thread on their own (unless I'm wrong? I'm practically a hermit on the internet, I don't know).
